why: In figures 2, 4 and 5 the small circle sits on a side edge of the square, at the middle height. In figure 1 the circle is moved down into the bottom-left corner, so it sits on two edges instead of one. The other figures keep the circle in the middle of a side, so figure 1 is the odd one. Figure 3 is a tempting choice because its circle is low and near the bottom-right corner, but it is only a mirror of figure 1, so it is not clearly different.
trick: For odd-one-out with a small circle on a border, check where it sits: middle of a side or at a corner, and which side. Compare the height first.
note: Ambiguous: circles in 1 and 3 are mirror images (both low near a bottom corner) while 2, 4, 5 are at mid-height of a side. No single clear odd one; option 1 chosen because it is the most corner-like.
